## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` runs `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py` in a nested pytest. On a macOS host under load (load average about 40-50), the nested run exceeds the 300 s per-test budget from `pyproject.toml`. The outer test then fails with a pytest-timeout. Under xdist in `make verify`, this showed up as a crashed worker (`gw3 ... Not properly terminated`).

## Observations (2026-11-03, merged tree b3d8ee49bb0)

- The outer test fails in isolation: rc=1, pytest-timeout.
- The 2 nested modules run directly: 14 passed in 318-360 s wall, with only about 8 s user and 16 s system CPU.
- `--durations`: each of 6+ tests in `test_opcert_service.py` spends 26-31 s in call. Examples: `test_server_never_pushes_and_workspace_is_isolated` 30.8 s, `test_plan_review_pass_signs_internally_and_returns_envelope` 28.2 s.
- CI (Verified +1 on Gerrit change 3277) passed the same test.

## Hypotheses (unproven)

- Each opcert service test waits on a fixed internal timeout or retry, such as a git fetch/push to an unreachable remote or a subprocess wait. That wait dominates its time, not CPU.
- Host contention alone stretches the subprocess-heavy setup.

## Approach

Profile 1 slow test (`py-spy dump` or `faulthandler` during the call) to find what it is blocked on. Fix that wait at its source, so the 2 modules finish well inside the 300 s budget on a loaded host. Do not raise the budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The blocking call behind the ~28 s per-test time is identified and recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py` completes in under 120 s on the dev host.
- [ ] The tortoise test passes in isolation on the dev host.
compiled_state.title: Opcert service tests idle ~28 s each; nested tortoise run exceeds 300 s budget
